name: Unique Custom Furniture
old_description: Each detail in our furniture has been lovingly handcrafted by our master artisans in Fredericktown, Ohio since 1995.
about:
Unique Custom Furniture is based in Fredericktown, Ohio, in Knox County. Founded in 1995 as a family-owned business, the company began when its owners started collecting barnwood from old barns in the surrounding area, refining and finishing the wood, and selling pieces at furniture shows.

The company designs and builds custom furniture from reclaimed chestnut and oak barnwood aged 100–200 years, sourced from Ohio, Appalachia, North Carolina, and Tennessee. The process involves kiln drying for two to four weeks, processing by an Amish wood specialist (planing, straight-line cutting, nail and dust removal), then in-house cutting, sanding, finishing, assembly, and quality inspection. Products include benches, buffets, tables, stools, dressers, hutches, office furniture, and media consoles.

Unique Custom Furniture serves residential customers and the broader furniture market, selling directly through its online store and producing custom pieces for individual clients. The company’s reclaimed barnwood furniture appeals to buyers seeking heirloom-quality pieces with historical character.

The founders were amazed at the beauty of finished old barnwood long before a barnwood furniture industry existed. They emphasize a unique aesthetic, a refined making process, and the use of genuine American barnwood handcrafted by skilled artisans, positioning each piece as a connection to American history.

name: United Manufacturers, Inc.
old_description: Since 1984, we at United Manufacturers have served as the leading manufacturer and provider of industrial accordion safety skirts for the USA and Canada.
about:
United Manufacturers, Inc. was founded in 1984 by Jeffrey and Anne Faris in Fond du Lac, Wisconsin. The company remains family-owned and woman-owned, now operated by the second generation—daughters Ali Faris Helleberg and Jenny Faris.

The firm specializes in custom contract sewing and industrial sewing, producing heavy-duty accordion safety skirts for lift tables, sewn bellows, private-label apparel, advertising specialties, sport bags, stadium cushions, gym uniforms, aprons, and hats. It also offers in-house screen printing, prototyping, product development, assembly, packaging, and fulfillment. Materials include canvas, nylons, fire-resistant vinyl, vinyls, and neoprene. The shop handles runs from small batches to large volumes.

Customers range from startups and entrepreneurs to large global corporations, with a focus on medical and safety products, healthcare providers, schools, and fundraising organizations. The company also serves promotional product distributors.

The founders’ vision was to deliver high-quality products with on-time shipments at competitive prices. United Manufacturers emphasizes no-charge engineering support for material, design, and specification recommendations, aiming to exceed customer standards through flexible production and personalized service.

name: United Plastic Molders
old_description: We are happy to say that we have had great success with some very influential companies throughout the years. Here are a few names you may recognize, including:
about:
United Plastic Molders, Inc. was founded in 1978 in Jackson, Mississippi, by William C. (Bill) Hoge, who remains the principal and actively oversees daily operations. The company began with six employees and four machines and has since expanded to six buildings encompassing more than 60,000 square feet.

The shop runs 24 molding machines ranging from 30 to 750 tons, operating around the clock five days a week, supported by a complete tool and die shop with four CNC mills. A staff of about 60 includes six expert tool and die makers, three molding technicians, and a maintenance director skilled in machine programming. Services cover injection molding, mold design and building, mold repair and inspection, prototyping, CNC machining, UV flatbed printing, and assembly and packaging.

Customers span a range of sectors, with client references including Black & Decker, Tyson Foods, Hobie Cat, Duck Commander, Peavey, and Porter Cable, among others. The company works with both large corporations and individual inventors, providing start-to-finish production from concept to packaged parts.

UPM emphasizes hands-on oversight by its founder, an in-house tooling team with decades of experience, and the flexibility to retrofit facility space, equipment, and storage to meet specific customer requirements. The business has grown largely through word-of-mouth referrals, highlighting a reputation for quality workmanship at competitive prices and on-time delivery.

name: United Semiconductors LLC
old_description: Producer and supplier of binary and ternary III-V semiconductors since 2005.
about:
United Semiconductors LLC was founded in 2005 in Los Alamitos, California. The company operates as a producer and supplier of binary and ternary III‑V semiconductor substrates.

The company specializes in bulk crystal growth of III‑V compounds, delivering polished, double‑sided wafers with diameters from 25 mm to 150 mm (1–6 in) and thicknesses of 0.5–10 mm. Its services span proprietary crystal growth, damage‑free wafer slicing and dicing (up to 75 mm), chemical‑mechanical grinding and polishing, high‑temperature impurity diffusion, activation and annealing (up to 1800 °C), and wet chemical etching, cleaning and passivation. It also produces research‑scale custom materials, nano‑inks (10–500 nm nanocrystals), luminescent powders, and optical components such as prisms and cubes.

United Semiconductors serves the microelectronics, optoelectronics, AI, space, and research sectors. Customers include researchers requiring small‑quantity custom synthesis, foundry partners for the company’s Optoelectronic AI Semiconductor Integrated Solutions (OASIS) Foundry, and organizations seeking space‑grown semiconductor crystals for radiation‑hardened devices.

The company emphasizes its proprietary crystal growth method, which yields uniform composition and high optical transmission with low defect density. It also highlights microgravity‑grown crystals for defect engineering and radiation hardening, and a damage‑free slicing process for both fragile and extremely hard materials.

about:
UnityPoint at Home operates a home medical equipment storefront Suite 107 in Des Moines, Iowa. The location is part of the broader UnityPoint at Home network, which provides durable medical equipment and respiratory services across the region. The input does not specify a founding year for this specific site, nor does it name individual founders or ownership structure beyond the UnityPoint Health system.

The Des Moines location functions as a retail and rental center for home medical equipment. Its offerings span respiratory therapy — including home oxygen, CPAP and BiPAP devices, and a PAP resupply program — as well as maternity and nursing supplies such as Medela and Spectra breast pumps, nursing bras, and maternity support belts. The store also stocks a range of durable medical equipment: canes, walkers, crutches, bathroom safety aids, blood pressure monitors, compression stockings, incontinence products, phototherapy units, rollators, transport chairs, TENS units, and over-the-counter orthotics. Staff assist customers with equipment selection, fitting, and ongoing service and maintenance.

The store serves patients recovering at home, individuals with chronic respiratory conditions, and new or expecting mothers. It accepts all Medicare and Medicaid patients, making it a key access point for beneficiaries seeking covered durable medical equipment. Customers include those referred by physicians for oxygen therapy, sleep apnea treatment, or post-surgical mobility aids.

UnityPoint at Home emphasizes the convenience of physical storefronts where patients can try equipment before renting or purchasing. The company highlights its experienced staff who guide customers through options and address questions, aiming to simplify the process of obtaining and maintaining home medical equipment.

name: Universal Packaging
old_description: Corrugated Packaging is our primary business, but we also offer
about:
Universal Packaging is headquartered in Duncan, South Carolina, and traces its roots to 1975 when John Houser and Charlie Muse left Owens Illinois to start Piedmont Packaging, a corrugated sheet plant in Spartanburg. In 1996 the pair launched Universal Packaging as a distribution-focused business from a 21,000‑square‑foot warehouse in Duncan. The company remains privately owned and today operates two facilities in Spartanburg County totaling 170,000 square feet.

The firm’s core business is corrugated packaging, but it also supplies poly film and bags, industrial foam, custom wood crates and pallets, protective non‑woven materials and bags, and provides assembly and kitting services. In‑house capabilities include CAD‑driven packaging design and sampling, ISTA testing, packaging review and performance assessment, and a 170,000‑square‑foot warehousing and inventory management operation supported by a company‑owned delivery fleet.

Universal Packaging serves a diverse customer base across the Carolinas. While the input does not name specific verticals, the breadth of materials and services suggests it supports manufacturers and distributors needing protective packaging, fulfillment, and distribution solutions.

The company was founded on a “Spirit of Cooperation” that emphasizes caring for employees and delivering “Relentless Service” to customers. That culture, combined with same‑day/next‑day shipping, owned transportation, and integrated design‑to‑delivery capabilities, is presented as its primary differentiator.
